title: Quickstrike rollout playbook pocket guide
content:
Summary:
Quickstrike is a compact, high-frequency rollout template for small feature sets (feature flags, model variant swaps, routing policy changes) intended to go from alpha to 100% in 5-8 business days with built-in safety gates.

Purpose:
- Provide a minimal single-page readiness checklist and KPI pocket dashboard for rapid rollouts.
- Emphasize measurable SLOs, fast rollback, and clear owner responsibilities.

Scope:
- Applies to hosted API feature flags, model routing changes, and Dedicated capacity configuration that affect inference surface area.

Pre-launch (owner: product-ops lead + eng owner):
- Stakeholders identified: product (owner), eng (owner), SRE, privacy/compliance if applicable.
- Ticket links: PRODOPS-482 (rollout plan), INFRA-1298 (capacity check).
- Safety smoke tests passing in staging: latency p95 < 250ms, error rate < 0.5% after 1h load test.
- Canary release gates prepared: canary toggle, metric collection, tracing.
- Communication: announce to #prodops-rollouts and set on-call for first 72h.

KPI pocket dashboard (measure every 10m first 48h):
- Request success rate (global, canary): target >= 99.5%; alert if < 99.0% for 10m.
- Latency p50/p95/p99 (global): p95 target <= baseline+20%; alert if p95 increases by >40%.
- Model output quality (sampled eval): baseline BLEU/ROUGE/QA-acc drop <= 2 points; alert if >3.
- Cost per 1k tokens: track delta vs baseline; flag if >+40% sustained 1h.
- User-facing errors (rate of 5xx): alert threshold 0.2%.

Rollout phases and guardrails:
- Phase A (Alpha, 1-2% traffic, 2 hours): smoke tests, basic metrics stable.
- Phase B (Beta, 10-15% traffic, 4-8 hours): load tests in parallel, UX sampling.
- Phase C (Ramp, 50% traffic, 24 hours): monitor cost and SLO drift, begin automated promotions if stable.
- Phase D (Full, 100%): final check then flip default toggle.

Rollback triggers and immediate actions:
- Trigger: error rate spike >1% sustained 5m or p95 latency >2x baseline for 10m.
  Action: flip feature flag to previous variant; post-mortem triage within 24h.
- Trigger: model quality regression >5% on sampled eval set.
  Action: pause rollout, divert canary to fallback model, open urgent triage with research.

Post-launch 7-day watch:
- Daily summary in #prodops-rollouts for first 7 days.
- 24h, 72h, 7d checkpoints: adoption metrics, regression checks, customer escalations.
- Decide to fully release, revert, or iterate (note owner and timeline).

Minimal runbook (first 30 minutes):
1) Confirm canary toggle is active and telemetry pipelines are green.
2) Verify sampling endpoints are collecting examples; snapshot samples to S3 (bucket: prodops-rollouts/snapshots).
3) Watch KPI pocket dashboard: success rate, p95, errors, cost.
4) If any gate fails, execute rollback procedure and notify stakeholders via Slack and PagerDuty.

Notes, quick heuristics and tradeoffs:
- If latency increases but error rate remains low, consider autoscale and temporary traffic cap rather than immediate rollback.
- For cost spikes driven by longer sequences, set per-request token cap as temporary mitigation.
- Keep customer-impacting thresholds stricter than internal ones.

Open questions / to-dos:
- Add automated quality regression alert tied to eval set (owner: applied-ml).
- Capture a small URL for the one-pager to share with sales engineering.

Appendix: Quick KPI snapshot CSV (collected every 10m):
timestamp,traffic_pct,success_rate_pctl,p95_latency_ms,cost_per_1k_tokens,5xx_rate,quality_delta
